questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Where the alphabet came from and how it spread
How young children learn their ABCs at school
How your surname's first letter may affect your life
Why teachers take the register in alphabetical order
questions.why: Neil says a surname later in the alphabet could be a disadvantage at school and in life.

questions.q: Why are the letters of the alphabet in their order?
options: The Romans chose it
No one really knows
They are in order of how common they are
Teachers decided it
questions.why: Neil says, 'no one really knows how the order became established.'

questions.q: Where does the problem begin, according to Professor Zax?
options: In university exams
In job interviews
When children learn to write their names
When the teacher calls names from the register
questions.why: The further down the roll call your name is, the less noticed you are.

questions.q: According to Professor Zax, what happens as the roll call goes on?
options: Everyone gets more excited
Attention and engagement get weaker
The teacher speaks more loudly
Students start to leave the room
questions.why: He says 'the intensity of the engagement diminishes'.

questions.q: Why do students whose names were already called stop paying attention?
options: They no longer need to take it seriously
They are talking to the teacher
They are doing homework
They didn't hear their name
questions.why: He says those already called 'no longer have any need to take things seriously'.

questions.q: When was the research on this disadvantage carried out?
options: In the UK in the 1990s
In Colorado last year
In the US in the 1950s
In ancient Egypt
questions.why: Neil says it was discovered after research in the US in the 1950s.

questions.q: Which disadvantage did the research find for people later in the alphabet?
options: They had more friends at school
They were more likely to become teachers
They were less likely to join the military
Their first jobs usually paid less
questions.why: Professor Zax says they 'had first jobs in occupations that paid less'.

questions.q: What does Sam imply when she says Professor Zax 'seems to have done OK'?
options: His surname starts with Z, but he's still successful
His research was wrong and nobody believed it
He had a very easy life because of his rich family
He changed his surname to get ahead in his career
questions.why: She adds 'Even with that surname!' and Neil says it doesn't apply to everyone.
